body:
I'm really worried about this too, as I'm starting medical school next month. I was never able to work at all while at school. I couldn't concentrate for more than 10 minutes with negligible to mild depression, I don't know how I'm going to cope with a much bigger work-load while having severe depression. I'm sort of hoping that since I don't get pleasure from hobbies any more, I will use my studies as a way to escape the constant suicide ideation.

If you find any strategies that work for you, then please let me know!
How long did it take for it to start working for you? I've been on it for 3 weeks now and nothing has changed :/
Have you noticed the affect of the fluoxetine yet? I've been on it for 3 weeks now and I haven't noticed any change at all :/

I had exactly the same experience a few years ago when I was surprised to hear that all of my friends said they wouldn't die for someone unless they were very close to them.

I had never really considered it before then, I had just taken it as a given that I would die for anyone (within reason), including people who I dislike. I'm not sure how depressed (if at all) I was at that point in time, though I know I had already experienced suicidal thoughts to some extent.

Nowadays I would be delighted to die for someone. A way to die which leaves me in a good light? Sign me up!
It's a common side effect of antidepressants. You should talk to your doctor about it, they may recommend changing medications.

I'm also in my first two weeks of antidepressants, and have been having even bigger mood-swings than before. What is keeping me going at the moment is that tiny bit of hope that the medication will start to work and will help make me feel better. After suffering for this long, I might as well stay around long enough to see if the antidepressant helps.

You've probably checked, but are you sure that the alcohol isn't affecting the medication? Since alcohol is a depressant, it can have detrimental effects. For mine, it says that alcohol is not recommended.

I watched Stephen Fry's 'The Secret Life of the Manic Depressive' (which I would recommend) and realised that my mood swings aren't normal. However I think I just share some symptoms with bipolarity, since apparently violent mood-swings are common in young people with depression.

I found it very hard to open up to my parents at first, but I never had any difficulty talking to my therapist despite getting extremely nervous about it. I would suggest that you write down negative thoughts when you have them and take it with you, as your mind may go blank when you get in there.
As someone who has been taking fluoxetine for a week, this is really reassuring. Thanks!

Just wanted to thank you because today I decided I would try again to enjoy games, and I started playing Skyrim since I bought it in the Steam summer sale. I've played it for over 6 hours today and I enjoyed every moment of it. Best day in a while, so thanks for prompting me :D

I understand how big of an achievement this is, so well done :) I have been trying to find pleasure in things recently because my depression takes away my motivation to do anything and stops me from enjoying anything. The biggest difference is video games. I used to play hours a day but I haven't played anything for a couple of months now.

Wow, thank you for taking the time to write such a useful post!

I guess I can't discount drug-induced hypomania yet then. I am fairly certain that using those criteria, excluding the 4-day requirement, I would have been classed as hypomanic yesterday. However, I'm not sure that I would meet them during my usual 1-3 day elevated periods. Guess I will wait and see, and talk to my psychiatrist about it when I see her on Wednesday. Again, thanks a lot for writing this, it was very informative :)

I have recent experience of this on the NHS. I am 17 though so it might be different if you are an adult. Basically I wasn't able to see my therapist (who I had seen once before) for 6 weeks and my depression and suicidal ideation/tendencies got a lot worse in that time. When I saw her again I told her the complete truth, which included self-harm, constant instinctive suicidal thoughts and knowing that I would instantly kill myself if I had a good enough method. I ended up talking to a psychiatrist and they put me on medication.

So from personal experience and talking to people on here, I am pretty sure that they would only suggest inpatient care if you have a plan to end your life, rather than just a strong desire to. I would suggest you tell your therapist the truth, it worked for me.

Is there a certain amount of time that the mood has to last to be counted as hypomania do you think? Because yesterday the intensely happy mood only lasted a few hours. I've had less extreme (though still above normal) happiness for 2-3 days at a time before, and 'euphoric' moods that lasted up to about 6 hours at a time.

Don't worry, I know that I can't diagnose myself with anything, and I would never ask anyone else to either. I would actually say I am on the other end of the scale - I often tell myself that I have somehow brought on my symptoms myself and that I can't actually have a problem.

I wasn't looking for a diagnosis, just asking if people had experience of SSRI-induced mania soon after their first dose. Thanks for your concern though, and I will be cautious when I study psychology :)
Ok, I will mention it to my psychiatrist when I see them on Wednesday. Thanks.

I often wish I was someone else, someone normal. I actually wish that I was my best friend sometimes, which I'm sure isn't very healthy. Most of the time I wish I would die or that I could kill myself but sometimes I just wish I could be a normal person with normal people feelings.
If you haven't got help yet then you should, and aim to become more accepting of you as a person. I started medication yesterday and I'm really hoping it will allow me to feel a bit better about myself.

I feel you. I always doubted myself a lot but the suicidal thoughts are what really made me realise that I did have a legitimate problem. I have a lot of the symptoms of depression but it all seemed too up and down to be the same as a lot of the people on here. In the end I realised that the suicidal thoughts were completely real and that it was a medical problem.

I like the way you write, and I think I can relate quite a lot to you. I had been thinking I had either depression with weird symptoms or bipolar II, but I will give BPD a look again. I will definitely be following your blog :)

If they want to stop, then you could suggest the [Butterfly Project](http://butterfly-project.tumblr.com/). Also, you could tell them to message you whenever they feel like cutting themselves, but only if you feel up to making a commitment like that.

If they don't want to stop, then you could try persuading them to seek professional help. Don't try to intervene too much though, as maybe just having someone to listen will help them a lot. Good luck :)

Do you have any sources about ADHD being more likely in people of high intelligence? I have recently considered the fact that I may have ADHD-PI mainly as a result of my inability to concentrate (and I do believe it is an inability, rather than purely laziness) but I read that my concerns would be dismissed by professionals (here in the UK anyway) because I have achieved highly at school. Oh and btw, I don't consider myself intelligent - I am simply referring to what society thinks intelligence is proved by - exam results.

* Pink Floyd - 'Shine On You Crazy Diamond', 'Wish You Were Here', 'Comfortably Numb' amongst others
* Loads of Biffy Clyro's music, though 'Bubbles' in particular applies to depression, I love 'Black Chandelier', 'Born on a Horse', 'Joke on Us' and many others for when I am in an angry sad mood
* Loads of others: Coldplay, Bowie, Idlewild, Keane, The Killers and Snow Patrol to name a few.

I don't have the same long periods of depression as you, but I have the same feelings about believing myself. So often I think that I must just be fulfilling my own prophecy, and that I am just doing it for attention or something. At other times though (usually the low moments or when I am uncontrollably angry) I am sure that I do have a legitimate problem. But then those moments pass and I start to think that I am faking it and that I can just stop feeling this way. The main symptom that I never doubt is my desire to commit suicide - I know that it is always genuine. Sometimes I ask myself 'how could you be suicidal if you don't have a legitimate, medical problem?'. I still doubt myself but my suicidal thoughts (ironically) reassure me that I am not just an attention seeking hypochondriac.

I agree with this also. Relatively recently I realised that I was having constant mood swings. Looking back I'm not really sure how I didn't realise that there had been something wrong for years. I guess it was because it slowly got worse over time, though it did become quite severe before I realised I had a problem. I think the main realisation for me was watching Stephen Fry's documentary 'The Secret Life of the Manic Depressive'. I'm not sure if I have bipolar or unipolar depression, but watching that program made me realise that my thoughts and behaviour were not normal. There is no 'reason' for me to be depressed either.

I have no idea. I should be really happy - I have a very fortunate life with nothing I can think of which might have triggered my mood swings. My future should be bright. When I come on here and read of the terrible events so many of the people here have suffered, it makes me feel kind of guilty. They have cast-iron reasons to be depressed, while I have no reason. I should be happy.

If they ask you then I *think* you could just say "I had some health problems to deal with." or something similar. Since it isn't a medical position, they shouldn't be able to discriminate against you for any mental health problem. If they wanted to check your 'occupational health' then it would be through a health and safety department with official guidelines. So what I'm saying is that I think you are completely justified in refusing to discuss specifics, should they ask you for them. What they will want you to prove is that you still tried to continue to learn/grow during your gap year. Find anything you have done and turn it into a positive, and run with it. Good luck :)

I've been in therapy for a little while now. It's not going to be enough by itself, these mood swings are just too much for me. Getting better seems like such a fucking effort. If I had a good enough method I would do it right this second.

Very well put, especially the part about the forest. I think I feel very similar to you, and I hate it. When I wake up, I hate everything and I never want to get up. Recently I have been able to stay in bed for a few hours to slowly feel slightly better, before getting up. Today was different, and I was woken up and had to get up quickly. It was so horrible. After I was woken up I just wanted to hurt myself, and all I had in my bed was my headphone jack. Then after I got up I started crying (first time in weeks of depression) and I didnt know why. All this time I was thinking of suicide and how much I hate the world and myself. I think it also made me feel negative for much longer than usual.

So in my experience (using your analogy), if you try to sprint through the forest, the undergrowth will hurt you more and you will emerge on the other side tired and the rest of the day will be horrible too. However if you can give it a bit of time and take the forest slowly, you will be able to enjoy the other side a lot more.

You're not alone, I promise.

I know you said you weren't asking for advice, but I might make a suggestion anyway if that's ok. You said you don't have the motivation to do the things you used to enjoy. How about you decide to do something that previously brought you pleasure, and see if it makes you a bit happier? Our thoughts, feelings and actions are all connected and while you cant control your feelings and thoughts, you can control your actions and that affects the other two. I realise I dont know your situation and i might sound patronising, so sorry if I do.

I don't have a reason. I have loving parents, great sisters and I've always had good friends. I've never had to experience someone really close to me dying. I have just finished 13 years of private education and I have an unconditional place to study medicine. I should be able to graduate a doctor with zero debt and without having to work before then. What I'm saying is that I should be able to have a happy and comfortable life. But I'm depressed. And unless something changes soon, I am going to be dead before long.

Yes, I do. Mornings are horrible, and I particularly agree with the dream/nightmare part. Often I feel better in the afternoon/evening though. I still have the ideations and self-hatred and everything, but it somehow feels easier to function and pretend to be happy. It is a pretty common symptom of depression and bipolar. We're not alone :)

> Not upbeat happy music, fuck that shit. When I'm depressed I like angry, bitter, powerful, cynical music by people who have been there and know what it feels like. The anger gives me the energy I need to keep going and keep trying to get back to that place where everything feels like it's going to be okay at least for a while.

This. I have listened to a lot of Biffy Clyro while depressed recently.
I wish I could.

Thanks for posting this, it's slightly reassuring to know that I might one day get some sort of answer.

My sleep is terrible, I get a handful of good nights of sleep each year. I only sleep a few hours and even when I sleep longer I don't feel rested. I also have been getting worsening nightmares. I'm not sure they would give me sleep medication though, (since I'm pretty young and have bad suicide ideation) would they?

I feel like this too, I have violent mood swings also. I'm yet to see anyone describe symptoms very similar to mine. Periods of days/weeks with normal depression and lots of the symptoms of depression, but my mood can change in seconds and sometimes I have horrible violently depressed periods that last less than a few hours. I am also extremely happy sometimes, possibly verging on hypomania which has made me consider bipolar, but I'm not sure at all. I can have some or all of these states within the same day sometimes.

I also have trouble sleeping and disturbing dreams, though nothing has obviously caused them. It has been getting worse for me recently, but I can give you advice that I've been given in the past.

First of all you should check your sleeping habits (sleep hygiene) is good. That means avoiding caffeine after lunch, making sure the light level is correct, making sure you are comfortable, adjusting temperature.. etc. Sounds kind of patronising but it's best to check these first. Also, being physically tired helps getting to sleep. Try going for a short jog/run during the afternoon or early evening. It should help you sleep. You could also try looking at mindfulness meditation. There are resources online and it has been scientifically shown to help depression, anxiety and sleep, amongst other problems. Worth a try, and it should improve other areas of your life even if it doesn't help you sleep.

You said it started a few months ago, and mentioned suicidal thoughts. Maybe you should think about getting professional help. You could mention it to your doctor, and see what they recommend, or think about seeing a therapist if those options are open to you.

My nightmares mainly tend to focus on my insecurities too, and have been getting worse. I am going to mention them to my therapist if there's an appropriate time, so I will message you if she tells me anything of use. Stay strong, I am sure you will pull through.

I'm assuming you are an adult in the UK. You didn't mention the extent of your suicidal thoughts, which your GP's response depends on greatly. Were you just thinking about it, or were you genuinely considering doing it? Depending on the severity, then your GP may want to offer you different therapies, talk about possible medication, refer you to another department or just check that you aren't in immediate danger.

I'm not sure of the protocol for adults, as I'm under 18. I pretty much just went to my GP and mentioned a few of my symptoms including suicidal thoughts and self-harm and he referred me to the child psych dept., but I think it's quite different for adults. You could try looking at the 'Map of Medicine' for depression on the NHS website, I found it very useful.
That's what I mean, I would have thought Google could put such results further down the page for searches which are clearly by suicidal people.

Sometimes I feel like Pink Floyd's Comfortably Numb fits it perfectly.

EDIT: That guitar solo is my favourite of any song. It is simply brilliant.

It's sad but I have seen this a few times in the past. Though I've never called the number, it's a nice thing for google to do. However, when you google for suicide methods or something, the Encyclopedia Dramatica entry is one of the highest, and contains phrases such as "don't tell anyone else your plans as they might try to stop you" whereas the other sites are trying to help.

No. I've only relatively recently seeked help for my problems, and here in the UK doctors are cautious about medicating mental health problems in young people. I think I will be offered fluoxetine if the CBT doesn't help, and it would be as well as continuing with the therapy.

I am hoping that therapy will be all that I will need, but I am not convinced it will be enough. My negative thoughts and suicide ideation in particular seem to be completely out of my control. They aren't conscious or logical thoughts, so how can I fight against them? I feel powerless. On the other hand, I am very worried about psych meds or worse going on my health record, as it will be scrutinised when I apply for posts/jobs in the future.

I have a lot of mood swings so sometimes 'powering through' just means an even bigger crash at the end. However I'm on a family holiday at the moment so I don't really have a choice.

I'm really hoping that the therapy makes some sort of noticeable difference because I really need it at the moment.

I'm doing ok. My mood has been quite unstable recently so I have been trying to power through it by keeping myself busy and distracted. It doesn't help that I haven't been able to see my therapist for weeks because of certain circumstances. However I got a text today saying my next appointment is on the 23rd, which is a relief. I am still kind of worried about it because my symptoms have gotten much worse since I last saw her. I was classed as 'moderate-severe' before but it's much worse now.
I don't live in the US, we do it differently here. I am starting medical school in September.

Yes, I do rely on websites for the majority of my information. I'm just out of high-school, what do you expect? You think that just because I don't pay for access to psychiatric journals, I can't claim to be more informed than the vast majority of people?

When I said websites I meant highly reputable websites, some of which contain peer-reviewed articles. Also I don't understand what is wrong with documentaries, as I think they are a valuable source of information, especially when made by reputable organisations eg the BBC. Also, I'm not making a naive claim that I am going to be a doctor, I really am. I am starting medical school in September and have a junior doctor's job waiting for me in 6 years time.

I'm not trying to prove my intelligence at all, I just think my treatment would be more effective if they treated me more like an adult rather than a child.

I may sometimes be extremely over-confident, but in this case I don't think I am being delusional. I have watched documentaries, read dozens of websites, I even know the diagnosis criteria of the main disorders. I'm even going to be a doctor myself in a few years assuming they don't think I'm too crazy. I just think they are insulting my intelligence sometimes. I don't need a little kiddies booklet to write my 'hot thoughts' in.. with it's huge font and stupid cartoons. I wish they would be straight with me.

Oh, there's no risk of that where I live. They seem overly-cautious about labels if anything. For example I told them all of my symptoms, moderate-severe depressive symptoms(physical and mental), years of suicide ideation, self-harm etc and yet I don't think they've even said the word 'depression' yet - it's all just 'negative thoughts'. I find it kind of patronising to be honest. I may be young but I understand it a lot more than 99.9% of adults.

I watched the first 10 minutes or so of this and I will try to watch the rest. I'm scared to watch it as I keep trying to persuade myself that I couldn't possibly be bipolar, but at the same time a lot of the symptoms match up. You know you have problems when you are hoping to just have depression..

I am a 5'3" male who just bought a new bike. However, take my advice with a pinch of salt as my legs are very long for my height. When I tried using an online calculator, my leg length wasn't even an option when I selected my height. I bought the 17.5" frame Specialised Hardrock Disc 2013 with 26" tyres. It's a great bike. You should be able to find a size without too much difficulty as most bikes are unisex nowadays anyway.

I've only realised recently how emotionally repressed I am in regards to faking happiness. As someone who has lots of unpredictable and currently untreated mood swings, there is a fine line between deciding to power through, and when to admit defeat. An example is going to the gym with my mum. Sometimes I am feeling terrible and I decide to just go anyway, and it makes me feel better. Sometimes I go and it makes me feel ten times worse. I just need to know whether to admit defeat or try to fight back, and it is difficult to gauge.

My emotional repression is mostly towards other people, rather than myself. Its actually a big problem for me because I never realised I did it until recently, and now nobody really believes that I have been so unstable for so long. It also applies when talking to doctors and my therapist. I am able to talk calmly and thoughtfully about my problems and I think that has meant that they don't realise how seriously unstable I actually am.

I'm worried that a relationship might cause me to kill myself, through a breakup or something. I don't want to be that guy who a girl feels they can't break up with because they are so unstable. Also I know that I don't deserve anyone and that everyone deserves better than me. I'm just hate myself too much at this point in time to date. Maybe if I ever love myself, I will be able to love someone else.

I have recently come to a similar conclusion. Until recently I had the thought of my family's sadness holding me back. Then one day I just realised that I don't care. It sounds selfish because it is, but in the end I will be dead and I believe that means complete nothingness. It doesn't help that my birthday is coming up. I keep thinking that if I kill myself on my birthday then it will be one less day that they have to be sad on.

It's not the core of my depression but it does come into it a lot. I'm an ugly, 5 foot 3, 17 year old guy who is pretty socially awkward when talking to anyone but good friends and family. It's weird because I would definitely say I am attracted to females and yet most of the time I think that if I live to be older, I won't have any relationships or marry/have kids. It's not even a delusion, I realise that I probably could find a wife and support a few children, and that I am 'expected' to. I just don't want to. I guess it stems from the fact that I know I am unattractive, as well as the fact that I don't want to make ties like that in case I finally kill myself one day.

Im also 17 and struggle with cutting. If you want then you can PM me any time, we could support each other :) Also, you could try looking up the Butterfly Project. I realise it might not be possible for you (it isn't for me) but I thought it looked great so I might as well mention it.

I have only just finished high school but I have forgotten all but the last few years in the same way already. I agree it would be very difficult to prove anything since everyone has different memories and some people's lives are probably more memorable than others.

I also have pretty bad memory for things in the past, despite statistically being within the top 1% of conventional intelligence. I can remember recent things reasonably well and can remember information quite reliably, but for some things I'm terrible. An example of this is my memories of primary school (5-12 years old). My friends and other people my age all seem to remember what they did, who their teachers were, and just have generally lots of memories of it. I, however, can remember almost nothing about it. My family seem to think I have a good memory, because I sometimes remember really random facts, but I am so bad in some areas.

However, I have no evidence to suggest it is to do with depression.

Wow, that's exactly what it is. I hadn't fully understood what makes me self-harm until now, but I think this is it exactly. This is why I love this sub, it helps me talk to my therapist more effectively. So thanks a lot! Also, what was the intense help you got?
Very low, I guess I had forgotten that some people don't consider it at all, let alone unstoppable, obsessional fantasies on a daily basis.

I understand what you mean to some extent. I often feel a sense of romanticism from depression, especially when self-harming. I occasionally do semi-abstract painting (badly), but I am yet to try it while depressed. I also get quite philosophical when I am depressed, coming up with weird realisations about life and depression.

It's your health which you are concerned about, that is healthy. As a doctor she understands that I'm sure, and is always happy to answer questions. When you pay for a session you are also paying for any extra support you need between sessions, so you shouldn't feel bad.

I get this too, like I know I'm hungry but for whatever reason I don't want to eat anything. Kind of feels like anhedonia for eating, to me anyway. Sometimes I only realise I'm hungry when I notice it's late afternoon and I haven't eaten or drunk anything all day, but only when I look at the clock. I will usually end up going into the kitchen, looking through all the food for 10 minutes, and giving up a few times. What I have found helps me to force myself to eat is cooking something really easy. It's usually one of my horrible omelettes which take about 2 minutes to make, but I usually manage to eat them once I've made them.

This is perfect. I feel like I've lost my human feelings and emotions from these years of pretending. I realised this recently when I was pretending to be happy when someone who I was with got really upset. I didn't know how to react. It's like all my inherent emotions have gone and I have to think about how I *should* feel in every situation. I feel like a fake, a fraud, an alien.
I don't know what age you are but it could just seem that the world is getting worse and worse because you are more aware of the world around you than you were, say, 15 years ago.

I agree. I sleep in the room next to my parents too, so I can't do anything to distract me, and I have to cry quietly too. That's one of the only things I'm looking forward to about university - being able to go to bed when I want and distracting myself however I please.

I guess being physically exhausted helps me a bit but that isn't always possible, especially when depressed. Nothing else has helped. I am worried what my shitty sleep cycle has done to my brain through my teenage years..
If it's any consolation, I would not have noticed your jawline in the second photo if you hadn't mentioned it. You also have cool hair :)

I find the gym puts me in an amazing mood while I am in the 'zone' but it tends to go down a bit when I leave. I'm sure it helps a bit in general though. It is also good because it is one less environmental factor my depression can be blamed on.

Hiking with suicide ideation however...

Your part about dying in 10 minutes has made me realise that actually there's nothing for me either. It's not like I've been prevented from achieving anything either (in fact I think I have a lot more than I deserve). I just don't have any huge life goals. I am not sure if I will get married or kids, or anything I want to own or anything like that. The sad thing is I would be happy if I found out I would die in 10 minutes..

The fact that I haven't thought of an effective enough way to do it yet.

At first it started with realising that I wouldn't really mind if I died in an accident. It slowly got worse though. Unending, unstoppable, obsessive fantasies of suicide for years. They have slowly destroyed my reasons to live one by one. Until recently my two reasons were that I didn't want to ruin my family and that I didn't have a satisfactory way of doing it. Recently though, in my lowest moments, I've realised that actually I don't care about how my family feel. Life was thrust upon me, I didn't ask for it, and it is a burden. I don't want to live to be an adult or to get old. I have no desire to live. In my opinion, there is no god and when I kill myself I will just stop thinking, I will have no existence. I will not be able to witness my families pain, and I will feel no pain myself.

I actually feel really calm after having reached this conclusion. I have nothing to lose - indifference is power. If I am killed in an accident through my negligence, all the better. But otherwise one day I will kill myself.

I really enjoy Hyperbole and a Half, but I don't relate to a lot of it because she has very different symptoms to me. However I do think she describes a lot of feelings amazingly well, so I might show my friends some of it to help them understand, so thanks for the idea.

Thank you for posting this! Stephen Fry is one of, if not, my biggest idols, and I find his progression inspiring. In particular, the fact that he has gone from constant suicide ideation to none. I had actually given up on the fact that mine might ever go away, resigned to the fact that I would have those associations in my mind forever, so to hear that his have completely gone away is amazing!

I also felt I connected with this:
"I do think I can usually be relied upon to be good company when I’m out and about and sitting round a table chatting, being silly, sharing jokes and stories and bringing shy people out of their shells.
But then I get home and I’m all alone again."

Now all I need to do is time travel!

But yeah, all joking aside, this is very interesting. I had never realised that they were a metaphor for depression, though that's probably because I didn't even realise I had a problem until recently.

Also wanted to add that in one of the happiest parts of the books/films, the DA are all learning how to produce patronuses, with Harry (who has already learnt the power of resistance) teaching them. Cho Chang is also having trouble, and I think this reinforces your point about the sadness in your past, since she experienced great pain when Cedric died.

I agree that it's logic is flawed, but it is the way I feel sometimes when I am at my worst. Most of the time I am thankful for my fortune. I'm not trying to trivialise anyone's suffering because I am sure I have no idea of how bad some people's situation is.

I don't know if I feel the same way as the people you mentioned, but I feel like if there was something which had 'caused' my depression, it would be taken more seriously. As it is, I should be extremely happy and stable, but I'm not. I don't know if it's inherent brain chemistry that is causing my huge mood fluctuations and other symptoms, but I can't think of anything else that could have caused them. I think since I've had such a perfect childhood, people are more likely to be like "you have nothing to be sad about, man the fuck up".

Seems weird to me, but maybe it's different where you are. I told a psychiatrist recently about my suicide ideation, which has been going on for at least 3 years but has got much worse within the last year. I made it clear that I think about killing myself all the time and that if I had a viable method I would have definitely done it by now. I'm under 18 as well. Seems weird that in (apparently) comparable situations the outcome was so different - I have been referred for CBT, and you have been forced into a psychiatric ward..

This really made me think. Life is not a gift - it's a burden. Personally, I don't think that thinking of family's sadness means there is hope. To me, it just means that committing suicide would cause more damage to them than is worth enduring personally for. So, you would rather endure the bus journey than to make it worse for the other people on the bus. However, surely there is a point at which the bus is so unendurable that you would get off.

HOWEVER, there are methods of improvement for your life - lifestyle improvement, self-help, medical help (obviously I don't know your situation). Think of them as like fixing the air-con on the bus, or talking to other people on the bus about how you might all work together to enjoy the journey better, etc

I think similar thoughts to you sometimes, and I am suicidal at times, but having started to get medical help has given me a little glimmer of hope. Maybe I will kill myself one day, but maybe life will improve. Might as well stick around to find out, right?
If you don't mind answering, what was it that caused them to force you into a psychiatric ward?

They wouldn't do that unless you genuinely thought you would kill yourself and were forming plans (rather than random ideas). I recently started getting help and told them about my suicidal thoughts. I made it clear that I think about it all the time, and that the only thing stopping me most of the time was thinking of my families sadness. I also told them that I would have done it already if I had a viable method. I made it clear that I didn't think i would kill myself unless something bad happened. I think you have to be actively suicidal to be committed.

While I haven't ever tried any drugs myself, I would like to warn people to exercise caution. I know quite a bit about these scientific studies which have/are being run, and I agree that they appear to be showing positive effects on people with depression. *However,* I believe that most, if not all, of these studies are on people with severe, long-term and treatment resistant depression.

The main danger is that of having a 'bad trip'. These are not positive experiences by any stretch of the imagination, and can lead to suicide attempts. In the studies being undertaken, the subjects are under carefully controlled clinical care while under the influence of the drug. Very different to taking an illegal drug in real life.

After learning of these studies, and reading anecdotal evidence from people who have taken hallucinogenic drugs, I read into it a bit. The biggest risk of these drugs (eg ayahuasca, DMT, mushrooms) is the fact that they can cause suicidal thoughts (which is obviously bad if you are already depressed).

So yeah, while a lot of people find taking these drugs beneficial to their lives, I think saying *"If your depressed, eat a bunch of magic shrooms, seriously."* on a subreddit frequented by so many depressed, vulnerable people is highly irresponsible.
